entries.text: Find a fuse in the west guest villa. Restore the generator beside the helipad. Recover the boat key from the powered lockbox in the main compound. Find fuel in the southeast boathouse. Return to the north dock.
I wrote this before I stepped off the boat. I do not remember writing the last line: “His..dih...so...bi-”
Y / TAB: backpack. J: collected files. The inventory and document reader pause the game. Keys and tools work only within reach of the object they fit.
Outbound: one service skiff. Fuel: insufficient. Ignition key: electronic safe, main villa. Spare generator fuse: west guest villa.
Someone has crossed out every passenger name. The pencilled total beneath the list has been changed from THREE to FOUR, then to THREE again. It reminds you of you're genocides.
A note on the reverse: “Do not wait for the fourth person. We watched him get on. WHAT DID I TELL YOU.”
The flashlight drains while switched on. Darkness stops the drain. A spare battery replaces the entire cell; do not waste it on a nearly full charge.
Candles are a backup, not concealment. A lit candle still gives away a person standing in an open lane. Matches can relight a candle, but they cannot restore burned wax.
The final sentence is pressed so hard into the paper that it has torn: “I found six used batteries inside the wall. Ughh... So tasty”
The marked rooms contain broken glass. Walk around it or crouch slowly across it. Moving over the shards upright causes cuts.
Bleeding slowly lowers condition and reduces your sprint. A clean bandage stops it and restores a little condition. A first-aid kit restores much more, because, well, it's a first-aid kit.
No dressing can help once a hunter has hold of your dih. Don't let them in the first place.
The upstairs supply crate is nailed shut. Use the crowbar from the ground-floor desk. Inside: rope, a cassette and a letter that was never delivered(they slow af).
Do not try to move the crate. The last worker who lifted it said something beneath the floor lifted with him.
We have stopped knocking on the boards to check whether they are empty. There is always an answer now.
The medicine cabinet is upstairs in the main villa. Its brass key was left on the desk upstairs in the west-lane house, beyond the first villa. A lockpick will also work, once.
Contents: one first-aid kit, a dry candle, and the night attendant’s report.
Every bottle in this cabinet has its label facing the wall. No one on the staff admits turning them around.
The boathouse supply case was chained shut after the last inspection. Bolt cutters are beside the crates in the generator shed.
The fuel can is outside the case. Do not waste time trying to cut its handle off. The case contains spare batteries and dressings for the return journey.
If the chain is warm, step back. We have no explanation for this.
I tied the handle shut from inside. It took longer to open. Four seconds, maybe. Long enough to count the breathing on the other side.
You can only brace a wardrobe while hiding in it. You need a fresh rope each time; leaving loosens the knot. Do not mistake a delay for an escape.
When the rope finally snapped, I heard someone inside the wardrobe behind me begin to laugh. There was no room behind me.
They follow the place a sound came from. Not the person who made it, unless they can still hear you or see your light.
Throw an empty bottle away from your escape route. The pocket recorder can play a short loop of footsteps as a decoy. It does not work while you hold it; place it and leave.
Do not follow a sound simply because it resembles your own footsteps. Especially if the ground is dry and the footsteps sound wet.
There are four hooks on the key board. Last night there were five keys. Tonight there are five hooks and no keys at all.
I opened every room on the inventory. The room numbered ZERO is not on any floor plan. A woman inside asked whether the boat had already left.
I told her there had never been a room zero. She answered from the room behind me.
We made rules because rules made it feel possible to leave. Never split up. Never answer the knocking. Never let the watcher see which wardrobe you choose.
I broke the first rule to find Jonas. He broke the second because the knocking used my voice. I do not know who broke the third.
If you find our notes, take them with you. A place is harder to forget when someone else knows its name. We were here. We were real.
All the clocks in the recovered photographs show 01:17. The lighting changes. The tide changes. The people in the photographs change places. The clocks do not.
At 01:18 the radio recorded forty-three minutes of silence. Under the silence is the sound of someone turning pages. NIGGANIGGANIGGANIGGANIGAGANIGNAIGNAGIANAINGAIGNA
The sealed records are optional evidence. You do not need them to start the boat. You may still want them when you reach the other shore.
[00:00] Wind. A boat engine turns twice and fails.

INEZ: “Mara, count us again.”
MARA: “Three.”
JONAS: “Then why are there four shadows on the dock?”
[00:19] Footsteps run away from the microphone. A fourth set of footsteps continues toward it.
INEZ: “Do not use this tape to call for help. It learned the loop. If you hear the next line before I say it—”

[01:17] A voice very close to the microphone: “Turn it off.”
[The tape continues for twelve minutes. Nothing else is recorded.]
There are fingerprints in the writing. Underneath, in much smaller letters: “It learns where you hide. Never let it watch you enter. EPSTEIN FUH NGAS RAHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH”
The paper is warm. The wall behind it is not.
A bundle of fictional shipping records, floor plans and photographs. Most names have washed away.
The last photograph shows the north dock from the water. A figure in the foreground is holding this same bundle. On the reverse is tomorrow’s date.
Take the records to the boat to carry the evidence off the island.
We counted six houses from the shore. There are more than six now. Jonas says the map is old. The houses behind us were not there when we arrived.
The footsteps climbed the stairs after me. I hid in the wardrobe. They crossed the room, stopped outside it, then continued above my head. This house only has two floors.
I stopped walking. The steps behind me stopped one beat later. I tried again. Same delay. Then something started walking in front of me.
The two figures by the empty houses turn toward every sound. Running brings them faster. Crouching buys time. Even when the light is out, they remember the last noise.
The man outside the window did not move for an hour. When I looked away he changed windows. When I watched him directly, he stepped back into the trees.
I left my backpack beside the bed and followed the knocking. There was no door at the end of that corridor. I can still hear my backpack radio from inside the wall.
Someone called from the other house. It sounded like Jonas, but his recorder was in my hand. The figure under the porch never spoke again.
I thought the watcher wanted me to see him. Now I think he was counting how many times I turned around. The knocks, the footsteps, the face at the window: all the same patient thing.
Mara went quiet in the upstairs room. We covered her and left the water beside the bed. I promised to come back with the boat key. I am still writing that promise.
If you find our things, do not follow the running footsteps. Find the fuse. Restore the generator. Take the key and fuel. Leave before the watching becomes something else.
Your narrow beam reaches across open ground. Hunters can see it. Check the charge before leaving a safe room.
A marked plan of the dock, villas and utility yard. The numbered route shows the supplies needed to launch the boat.
A small folding blade. Cut clean fabric from an open wardrobe to make two emergency bandages. Each wardrobe has only one usable piece.
A sealed replacement cell. Restores the flashlight to full charge. Replace it before the beam dies in the wrong room.
Stops bleeding and restores 15 condition. Broken glass cuts moving feet; crouch to cross it carefully. A bandage cannot save you from a hunter’s grip.
Dressings and antiseptic. Stops bleeding and restores 55 condition. Save it for a serious injury.
Levers the nailed boards off a supply crate. The noise carries through nearby rooms. Look for the boarded crate in the west villa upstairs.
Cuts the chain around the boathouse supply case. Too heavy to use quietly. The blades are marked with dried red dust.
Opens a small cabinet lock when the brass key is missing. The cheap tension wrench bends after one successful use.
A small key stamped STAFF. It fits the medicine cabinet in the main villa upstairs.
Tie the wardrobe handle from inside. A hunter who watched you enter will take four extra seconds to force it. This buys time; it does not make the wardrobe safe.
Throw it in the direction you are looking. It breaks against the floor or the first wall, giving listeners a sound to investigate. Move away before they arrive.
Listen to a collected cassette in Files, or place a looping footstep decoy up to eight metres ahead. It lasts twelve seconds, then needs twenty seconds to reset.
A recording of the failed crossing. Play it with the pocket recorder to save the full transcript to your document archive.
A match lights a candle. Relighting an extinguished candle costs another match. Keep the box dry.
Ninety seconds of dim, warm light within nine metres. Requires a match to light. Hunters can see this light too. F extinguishes it.
Fits the generator in the utility yard beside the helipad. Installation consumes the fuse and restores power to the boat-key lockbox.
The north-dock boat’s ignition key. You also need fuel before the engine will start.
Enough fuel for the crossing. Carry it back to the boat on the north dock.
Fictional, water-damaged records recovered from the pavilion. Taking them off the island changes the ending.

MAINTENANCE LOG / 00:43
The lights went out.
“Spare fuse is here in the maintenance hut. Generator is beside the central helipad. Once power is back, the key safe in the main villa should open.”
“Fuel cans are in the southeast boathouse. One last thing: Epstein can see the flashlight. Switch it off before he closes in. The dark hides you, but he remembers where you were. Move quietly.”
